focus: A1 session-to-packet binding: enumerate binding mechanisms with their session and packet failure modes
noveltyJustification: All 6 findings are new to this lineage: the packetless scope key, the fail-closed identity contract, the cwd-only repo-root walk, the offer-never-calls-tool default, the runtime-dispatched (not packet-dispatched) set path, and the grep-proven absence of any goal.md consumer.

ruledOut.approach: Derive the packet from the objective string (dereference a path in the objective)
ruledOut.reason: The plan YAML fixes objective shape as pointer plus copied criteria, never a file body, because nothing dereferences a path in an objective; a dereference would sit on every surface and every cap.

ruledOut.approach: Use the legacy singleton active-goal.json as the session-to-packet binding
ruledOut.reason: The hook README classifies it as diagnostic input only and never an injection fallback.

summary: The goal scope key hashes workspace+runtime+sessionId only; the packet is absent from goal identity and goal.md is not an input to any read or mutation.
Identity is mandatory and fail-closed (MISSING_SESSION_ID, MISSING_RUNTIME, INVALID_RUNTIME); a runtime without a native session identity cannot bind at all.
Workspace resolution walks up to .git or .opencode/skills and never infers a packet from cwd; there is no nearest-packet mechanism in the core today.
speckit plan defaults to offer and calls no goal tool in any runtime; set requires an explicit choice plus goal_objective.
The goal set path dispatches by runtime (opencode tool, pi CLI with native scope flags, cursor handoff, default native command) and never carries a packet path.
Objective shape is explicitly non-dereferencing and a repository grep finds no runtime consumer of goal.md; only spec-kit validation, templates, docs, and tests mention the file.

direction: Derive the packet from a path embedded in the objective string
reason: The objective contract forbids a file body and assumes nothing dereferences an objective path.

direction: Use the legacy singleton active-goal.json as the binding source
reason: Documented as diagnostic input only, never an injection fallback.
